text:
anya: quick idea > small helper to attach a compact deploy annotation + optional pin + change-window and auto-draft release PR. aim: reduce back-and-forth when product and ops need context.

miguel: show example CLI?

anya: prototype usage:
```
/deploy annotate \
  --sig llm-encoder-cost-opt \
  --pin model=encoder-3.2.0 \
  --pin-mode append \
  --window tomorrow/2h  # shorthand: start tomorrow 09:00 for 2h or use RFC3339 range
  --auto-rollback 3%:5m \
  --canary-source prometheus:embed-enc-canary \
  --notes-template short \
  --notify team \
  --idempotent \
  --dry-run
```

deploy-bot: preview created: annot-3500011111 (dry-run). preview text: "sig: llm-encoder-cost-opt | pin: encoder-3.2.0 | window: tomorrow 09:00-11:00 | auto-rollback:3%/5m"

ops-oncall: can parser accept calendar aliases? e.g. `calendar:team-release` so it auto-maps to our shared change window? timezone handling important

anya: yes parser supports RFC3339 ranges, relative shorthands (inNh, tomorrow), and `calendar:<name>` alias. will default to UTC but show local times in preview based on channel timezone.

miguel: PR behavior: if `--notes-template` used or `--notes-file` omitted, bot should create draft PR with a short YAML blob in the body for downstream tooling to consume. example YAML:
```yaml
sig: llm-encoder-cost-opt
summary: tweak cache policy to reduce long-context cost
checks:
  - smoke: ok
  - canary: 15k reqs <3% err
  - rollback: auto(3%/5m) enabled
notes_link: https://git.redwood/release-notes/3500
```

release-sheriff-bot: canary hookup available via `--canary-source=prometheus:embed-enc-canary`. also support `--canary-metric` override (defaults to error_rate).

ops-oncall: edge-case  what if pin is a range like `encoder@^3`? we should warn and require `--force-range` to proceed. also default `--pin-mode=append` to preserve history.

anya: agreed. will implement validation: exact version allowed by default; semver ranges require explicit acknowledgement. idempotency: `--idempotent` ensures repeated annotate calls merge instead of creating duplicate pins/PRs.

miguel: UX: Slack preview should include an expand button showing the YAML and two actions: [Create PR] [Cancel]. on Create PR we run preflight hooks (lint, smoke tests, canary warmup) and only create draft PR if preflight passes; if preflight fails bot posts failure summary.

ci-bot: recommend adding `--ci-check` to gate creation on a successful CI run for the change branch.

anya: good idea. I'll add `--ci-check` and `--quiet-on-success` flags to reduce noise for routine hotfixes. flags list for RFC: `--sig, --pin, --pin-mode, --window, --auto-rollback, --canary-source, --canary-metric, --notes-template, --notes-file, --no-pr, --notify, --quiet-on-success, --dry-run, --idempotent, --ci-check, --force-range`

miguel: I'll draft the RFC with a small flow diagram and sample Slack screenshots. will include tests for idempotency and rollback triggering.

anya: I'll open the bot PR and a small releases repo PR creator. plan: feature-flag behind beta group for a week, then enable org-wide if no issues. assigning @release-sheriff-bot to validate prometheus hook and @ops-oncall to sanity-check calendar tokens and timezone conversions.

ops-oncall: ack. will also verify that notify levels map to the right channels (team vs channel vs quiet) and that audit logs include the pin-mode and who applied it.

miguel: nice. once RFC lands we can iterate on templates for longer release notes and add an API for programmatic annotation from CI workflows.

anya: thanks all — opening RFC in ~20m.

migrated-bot-note: this conversation will be referenced from `design/deploy-annotator` in the RFC.
